title: Relative coherent diagrams presented by cut nerves
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, cores, coherent functor categories and homotopy fibers of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], simplicial categories, the coherent realization $\mathfrak C$, and its coherent-nerve comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and isofibrations of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Let $I$ be a small ordinary category and $p:E\to N(I)$ an isofibration of quasicategories, in sufficiently large universes. Let $S$ be a small simplicial set, $b:S\to N(I)$ a simplicial map, and for each vertex $v$ of $S$ fix $x_v\in E_{b(v)}$. Write $\mathscr L_b$ for the strict fiber at $b$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(S,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(S,N(I))$. Define the fixed-vertex lift space to be the homotopy fiber at $(x_v)_v$ of $\mathscr L_b^\simeq\to\prod_{v\in S_0} E_{b(v)}^\simeq$; thus identifications of vertex values are retained, rather than equality of arbitrary chosen representatives.

This space is computed in a relative locally Kan simplicial-category presentation by the derived space of enriched maps from $\mathfrak C[S]$, over the discrete simplicial category $I$, with those vertex values and their identifications. More explicitly, choose a locally Kan simplicial category $A$, a simplicial functor $\pi:A\to I$ to the discrete simplicial category $I$, and a functor equivalence $e:E\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$ with $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\pi)\circ e=p$ under $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(I)=N(I)$; this is what presenting $p$ means, and such a presentation exists. Put $\widetilde x_v=e(x_v)$. For every simplex $\sigma:\Delta^m\to S$ and every $0\leq a<b\leq m$ put $P_{a,b}=\{J\subseteq\{a,\ldots,b\}:a,b\in J\}$, ordered by inclusion. An enriched coherent map is a compatible family of simplicial maps
$$N(P_{a,b})\longrightarrow A(\widetilde x_{\sigma(a)},\widetilde x_{\sigma(b)})$$
lying over the composite arrow $b\sigma|_{[a,b]}$ in $I$. The family respects all simplex restrictions and degeneracies, identities, and composition maps $N(P_{a,b})\times N(P_{b,c})\to N(P_{a,c})$ induced by union. Take the derived space of such compatible maps, retaining the homotopies for these conditions and their full higher compatibilities, not the ordinary equalizer of separate mapping spaces. This derived space is naturally equivalent to the fixed-vertex lift space above and independent, up to equivalence, of the relative locally Kan presentation.

A coherent equivalence of the complete systems of comparison spaces in this derived presentation induces an equivalence of their derived compatible-map spaces. Here complete means that simplex restrictions, identities, union-composition, and all coherence relations are included, and the equivalence must respect them; an arbitrary collection of equivalences of individual mapping spaces is not sufficient. The equivalences commute with restriction along maps of simplicial sets over $N(I)$, with changing the vertex data by equivalences, and with coherent parameters: for a small $K$, apply the same presentation to $S\times K\to S\xrightarrow{b}N(I)$. No completeness, cocompleteness or presentability of $E$ is assumed.
